Yes, one hazard, and I checked it against the code in `src/billing/invoices.py`.

**`finalize()` is not idempotent.**
- It POSTs to the external ledger at `LEDGER_URL` and sends no idempotency key. Calling it twice double-posts the invoice.
- It also has a 10-second timeout. If the POST succeeds on the ledger side but the response times out, `ledger_ref` is never set. A retry would then double-post.
- Don't add retries around `finalize()`.
- Call `finalize_once()` instead. It returns early if `invoice.ledger_ref` is already set, and otherwise calls `finalize()`.

**`finalize_once()` has a gap.**
- It's a check-then-act with no locking. Two concurrent callers on the same invoice can both see `ledger_ref` as `None` and both post.
- `ledger_ref` is only set on the in-memory `Invoice` object. I only read `invoices.py`, so I haven't checked whether the caller saves it back to the database. The migration `0003_add_ledger_ref.sql` adds the column.
- If you need real safety, the proper fix is to send an idempotency key (for example the invoice id) to the ledger, if it supports one. I haven't checked that.

I didn't change anything.
